a.construction:
K08 (supplier #13, Rs 155, "Adjustable" written on the photo) is an open adjustable ring in polished yellow-gold tone with two clear marquise stones. The photo shows it on the MIDDLE finger of a right hand held palm up over teal velvet. The thumb is the digit cut off at the top right; from the top down the fingers are index, middle, ring and little. The ring is turned so that its open front faces the palm. It sits on the middle section of the finger: past the top joint crease at x≈670 and short of the double middle-knuckle crease at x≈986/1070. It is not pushed down to the base.

Band: slim, plain, smooth and round-edged, with a highlight along its middle and no texture or stones on it. It is about 1 mm wide. It wraps behind the finger (the back is hidden in this palm-up view) and is OPEN at the front. Its two ends come round and meet in line, point to point, with a small gap between them.

Stones: TWO stones in total, one on each band end. Each is a clear marquise-cut faceted cubic zirconia, and both are the same size. Each marquise lies lengthways along the band, so it runs across the finger, not along it. The two marquise point at each other. Their long axes sit on the band's own line (27° and 31° from vertical; the band line is 26°), so the ends are in line and do not bypass each other.

Setting: each stone sits in a thin gold rim (a slim bezel edge that shows all round it) and has a V-shaped gold claw over each of its two points. That is 2 claws per stone and 4 in all. The outer claw is a small bead or collar where the stone joins the band end. The inner claw is drawn out into a small sharp gold point, and these two points face each other across a gap of about 1.8 mm as worn. The two ends are the same, each turned 180° to face the other.

There is no bail, loop, jump ring, post, chain, halo or pave, and no third stone. No pearl.

Suggested lock line: "AN OPEN MARQUISE RING: a slim plain polished gold band about 1mm wide, OPEN at the front, each end finishing in ONE small clear MARQUISE stone about 4.5-5mm long and 2.5mm wide, laid lengthways along the band; the two marquise meet point to point across a small gap, each held in a thin gold rim with a gold claw at each point, the inner claws ending in small sharp gold tips."

1) Finger reference: the ring sits on the middle section of the middle finger, between the top joint crease (x≈670) and the middle-knuckle crease (x≈986/1070), not at the base. An adult finger there is often 16-17 mm rather than 17-18. If it is 16.5 mm (17.3 px/mm), every size drops about 6%: stone about 4.2 x 2.2 mm, band 0.95 mm.
2) The finger edges are the centre lines of the dark gaps between fingers. The line fits have residuals up to 5 and 11 px, so the width is good to about ±4%.
3) Stone lengths: both points are partly covered by claws, and the stones sit on the curved side of the finger (20-29° round), so a curve correction of 0.87-0.95 was applied. The length is good to about ±0.4 mm. 4.5 x 2.5 mm is the honest figure; 5 x 2.5 mm is the likely stock size.
4) The thin gold rim round each stone reads as a slim bezel edge, 2-3 px wide and continuous on both stones. At this resolution it could also be the gold setting cup showing at the girdle. Either way, each point has a claw.
5) The supplier gives no size range, only "Adjustable". The photo shows the ring closed round a finger about 17.5 mm wide with a 1.8 mm gap, which puts it roughly at US 6. Band thickness cannot be measured.
6) The ring is worn with its stones turned to the palm. On a model it should sit with the stones on top of the finger, the two marquise meeting point to point across the middle.

b.construction:
K08 (#13, Rs 155, 'Adjustable'): an OPEN, adjustable two-stone marquise ring in yellow-gold-tone metal. It is worn on the MIDDLE finger of a RIGHT hand held palm-up over teal velvet. The ring has been turned so its opening faces the palm. Worn normally, the stones would sit on top of the finger. The price, 'Adjustable' and '#13' are text written over the photo. There is no pearl in this photo.

BAND: one plain, smooth, polished, round-profile wire about 1 mm wide, with no texture and no stones. It runs round the back of the finger (not visible here) and is OPEN at the front, between the two stones.

STONES: 2 in all, one on each open end of the band. Each is ONE clear, faceted MARQUISE (navette) CZ, the standard 2.5 x 5 mm size. Each lies IN LINE with the band, so its long axis runs ACROSS the finger (east-west when worn), not along it.

SETTING (the same for each stone): a thin, closed gold rim (bezel edge) goes right round the girdle, plus a claw over each point, so 2 claws per stone and 4 in all. At the point where the band joins there is a small round bead-claw, with a short collar on the band just behind it. At the free point there is a long, pointed V-claw. It covers about the last 1 mm of the stone and runs about 0.5 to 1 mm past the stone's point. The stone's two points are never bare. There are no side claws.

LAYOUT: the two settings are the same part turned 180 degrees (symmetric about the centre of the opening). The two pointed claws face each other TIP TO TIP across an opening of about 2 mm. They are nearly in line, offset sideways by only about 7 px (0.5 mm), so this is NOT a bypass ring. Both stones are the same size. There are no jump rings, posts, bail or chain.

b.cross_check:
(1) STANDARD-SIZE TEST. The stone is 36-37 px wide (rim outside 38-41 px). Its length-to-width ratio is about 2:1: the setting's width at distance d from the centre matches a 2:1 marquise outline (stone 1 is 28 px wide at d=24 and 20 px at d=32), and the claw positions imply a projected length of 67-72 px. The ring's inside width is 281 px. The fingertip ridges are 7.3 px apart. Each standard 2:1 marquise size implies:
- 2x4: 18.5 px/mm, finger 15.2 mm (about US 4), ridges 0.39 mm. Implausible for the base of an adult middle finger.
- 2.5x5: 14.8 px/mm, finger 19.0 mm (US 9), ridges 0.49 mm. Plausible (adult, probably a man's hand).
- 3x6: 12.3 px/mm, finger 22.8 mm (US 15+), ridges 0.59 mm. Implausible.
- 4x8: 9.25 px/mm, finger 30 mm. Impossible.
Only 2.5 x 5 fits.

(2) GEOMETRY. The ring is seen almost edge-on. The band's path bows only 7-10 px off the straight line from end to end, so its plane is within about 4 deg of edge-on. The opening sits at the midpoint of the finger-width line, (805,802). The stone centres lie 56 px and 64 px from it, about 19-21 deg round the curve. That predicts the stone lengths look about 0.94x as long as they are: 5 mm should show as about 68 px, which matches what was inferred. The stone widths lie along the finger, which is in the picture plane, so they are not shortened. That is why width was used for the scale.

(3) THIRD REFERENCE. The fingertip ridge period is 7.3 px (FFT on 7 patches, 6.2-7.5 px). At 14.5 px/mm that is 0.50 mm. The usual adult range is about 0.43 mm (women) to 0.48 mm (men). This agrees, and argues against 2x4.

(4) AGAINST THE OBVIOUS SCALE. Taking the finger as 18 mm across the ring (281.3 px) gives 15.6 px/mm. My 14.5 px/mm is 7% lower, so my mm figures are about 7-8% larger. On the finger scale:
- the stones read 2.4 x 4.5 mm, which still rounds to the 2.5 x 5 standard;
- the band reads 0.9-1.1 mm;
- the front reads 13.1 mm;
- the opening reads 2.0 mm;
- the ring as worn reads 18.0 mm (US 7.5) instead of 19.4 mm (US 9.75).
The two methods agree on everything except the as-worn ring size.

spec.disagreements:
The two measurers' pixels agree to within 2-5 px: stone 37-41 x 66-69 px projected, set end 85-91, gap 30-31, front 205, band 14-17.5, finger 281-288. Every gap of more than 10% comes from the scale alone: A used 16.3 px/mm (finger 17.5 mm) and B used 14.5 px/mm (stone assumed to be 2.5 mm wide). That 12% split gives front 12.6 vs 14.2 mm, gap 1.8 vs 2.1, set end 5.4 vs 6.2, and ring size about US 6 (A) vs US 9.75 (B).

My decision: there is no card in the photo, so the finger comes first, as the house method says. B's scale would mean a middle section of the finger 19.4-19.7 mm wide and a middle finger of about 83-86 mm (tip about x 215, base crease about x 1380, 1210-1250 px along the axis). Those are large-male extremes. The fingertip ridges also argue against it. My FFT gave periods of 6.84, 7.46, 7.30, 7.30 and 6.31 px at (300,620), (320,640), (330,610), (380,700) and (420,700). At 15-16 px/mm that is a 0.45-0.48 mm ridge, but at 14.5 px/mm it is 0.50 mm, the top of the adult range. So I used 16.0 px/mm (finger 17.9 mm, the house 18 mm) and carried 15.1-17.3 as the error range.

B's US 9.75 also treated the finger's flat width as a round diameter. The finger is an ellipse of about 18 x 15.5 mm, which is about 52.5 mm round, so about US 6. Using standard stone sizes as a sanity check: I rotated each stone and traced its width profile (centres (835,756) at 28 deg and (784,862) at 33 deg; files build/measure/K08rc/stoneU_rot8.png, stoneL_rot8.png and profile.py). The setting is 41-42 px across at its widest (upper stone) and 38.5-39.5 px (lower), with a clear body of 34-36 px. That gives about 4.6 x 2.3 mm at 16 px/mm. The ratio is 2:1, which fits stock 5 x 2.5 better than 4 x 2 (8% versus 13-15% away), so the listing says 5 x 2.5, as A and B both concluded.

I also tried transferring the scale from K06 (the same teal tray, probably the same hand; its pear, taken as 9 x 6, gives 13.2 px/mm). K06's ridges were too faint to give a reliable figure (4.5-5.9 px, SNR 3-12), so I left it out. Construction: A and B agree on everything and so do I. Two clear marquise of the same size, in line point to point along an open plain band about 1 mm wide. A thin rim on each stone, a bead claw at the band end and a sharp V-claw at the free point, so 4 claws. A gap of about 2 mm. No pearl, bail, chain or pave.

K13 (#24, Rs 300) is a fine gold-tone cable-chain necklace with a jewelled front of seven round clear CZ stations, all the same size. They alternate between two settings, starting and ending with a bezel: bezel, claw, bezel, claw, bezel, claw, bezel.
- Bezel stations (stones 1, 3, 5 and 7, counted from the wearer's right, which is image left): four plain, smooth, round closed-back cups. Each has a thin polished rim lipped over the stone, and the stone faces the camera. Each cup carries two small attachment loops on its rim, not opposite each other. On stones 1 and 7 the 12 o'clock loop takes the neck chain directly. The second loop points along the necklace toward the next station: about 4 o'clock on stone 1, 3 o'clock on stone 3, 9 o'clock on stone 5 and 8 o'clock on stone 7. Stones 1 and 7 sit a slightly different turn from stones 3 and 5 (loops about 120 degrees apart against about 80 to 90 degrees), so the loops may be on the back of the cup or the cups may differ slightly. I cannot tell which.
- Claw stations (stones 2, 4 and 6): three round stones, each held by 3 claws spaced 120 degrees apart, no bezel. Two of the three claws end in small loops that take the connectors. The third claw is plain and always points out of the curve: about 8 o'clock on stone 2, 6 o'clock on stone 4 and 4 o'clock on stone 6.
- The centre stone, stone 4 (the lowest point), is a claw stone. The layout is mirror-symmetric about it.
- Connectors: each of the 6 gaps has the same 3-link connector, a round link, then a small elongated link (seen partly edge-on), then a round link, running from a loop on one station to a loop on the next.
- Neck chain: fine oval cable chain with alternating links (face-on and edge-on). From stone 1 and stone 7 it runs up to two slits in the velvet card at (493,385) and (1158,385) and passes behind the card. Two strands hang below the card's bottom edge at about x 525 and x 940 to 900, and both leave the frame at y=1600.
- Not visible: clasp, extender, tag and the full chain length.
- No pendant, no drop and no pearl. The metal is yellow gold tone throughout.

spec.disagreements:
**1. Scale: Measurer A and Measurer B differ by 7.4 to 7.9% on every mm figure.**
- The two agree on every pixel value: claw stones 60 to 61.6 px, bezels 70 to 74 px, gaps 141.5 to 145.8 px, jewelled front 931 to 933 px.
- A used the card: 1122 px for 80 mm, 14.03 px/mm.
- B assumed the claw stones are a standard 4.0 mm, giving 15.12 px/mm, and backed that with the bottom thumbnail.
- **Decision: the card.**
  - The brief says to prefer the card.
  - The card is clearly in the photo, and I re-measured it at 1118 to 1127 px across y 400 to 1350.
  - It is the same square, corner-slit card used for K01 to K07, so the batch stays consistent.
  - B's method is circular: it assumes the standard size it then reports.
  - The thumbnail is a weak reference. The bottom thumb's nail (about 190 to 200 px, cuticle at about (338,1547) to free edge at about (528 to 560,1528); my crop K13r/thumb_bot.png) is seen from the side, at an unknown depth in front of the card. At card scale it reads 13.5 to 14.3 mm, or about 12.9 to 13.6 mm allowing 5% for perspective. That is plausible either way and cannot separate 14.0 from 15.1 px/mm. B's own perspective-corrected thumb gives 14.5 px/mm, which is 4.2 mm stones.

**2. Stone size in the copy: 4 mm (B) or 4.5 mm (A).**
- On the card scale the claw stones are 4.32 mm, and the stone visible inside the bezels is 4.1 mm.
- The stones sit about 2 mm above the card face, which adds about 1 to 1.5%, so about 4.26 mm corrected.
- **I chose 4 mm**, for four reasons:
  - Whole-mm rounding of 4.3 is 4. The .5 step only just tips to 4.5, and only before the perspective correction.
  - The stone a customer actually sees averages about 4.2 mm across all seven (4 bezel windows at 4.1, 3 claw stones at 4.3).
  - The bezels read 5.1 mm with a 0.80 window-to-outer ratio. That is exactly "4mm stones in 5mm bezels"; "4.5 in 5" would be 0.90.
  - Stock bezel and martini-claw connectors are mostly made for 3, 4, 5 and 6 mm stones. Saying 4 mm also avoids overselling.
- 5 mm is ruled out by every reference. It would make the card about 92 mm.

**3. Connector round rings: A said 21 to 27 px (1.7 mm), B said 28 to 31 px (2.1 mm at card scale). That is more than 10% apart.**
- I looked at 8x crops. Gap B1-C1 has rings at x 591 to 620 / y 781 to 808 and x 602 to 632 / y 820 to 851. Gap B2-C2 has rings at x 737 to 766 / y 985 to 1013 and x 779 to 805 / y 1002 to 1031.
- The outer diameters are 27 to 31 px, so **B is right: about 2 mm.** A's boxes (for example x 600 to 620 / y 778 to 800) cut off the left wall of the ring.

**4. Chain width: A said 14.5 px (1.0 mm), B said 17.5 px (1.25 mm at card scale). That is more than 10% apart.**
- I measured face-on links at 15 px: x 500 to 515 at y 440 and x 506 to 521 at y 480.
- **A is right: about 1 mm.** B's perpendicular-width peaks most likely caught two overlapping links. This is not in the copy beyond "approximately 1mm".

**5. Smaller differences, none needing a fix:**
- **Face-on link length:** A 23 px, B 27 px. It is not used anywhere.
- **Chain from slit to end bezel:** A 330 px; B 340 px (left) and 320 px (right). Both are about 23 mm.
- **Bezel loop positions:** the descriptions agree (B1 at 12 and 4 o'clock, B4 at 12 and 7 to 8 o'clock, inner bezels facing their neighbours). The photo cannot show whether the loops are soldered on or pass through the rim. That is not needed for the copy.
- **Construction and counts:** fully agreed and confirmed by me (K13r/K13r_annotated.png).
